messages:
Anya Patel: heads up — after kernel-selection rollout (commit a1b2c3) we're seeing ~12-15% drop in prefix cache hit rate on private deployments for the gpt-small profile.
Mike Chen: do we have hit-rate numbers by bucket? hosted vs dedicated vs private?
Anya Patel: yes — hosted 78%, dedicated 72%, private 63% (7d moving avg). logs: /logs/prefix_cache/1840111222/summary.csv
Jordan Lee: interesting — any config diffs? prefix_cache_version, normalization flags?
Priya Singh: i checked — private had prefix_normalize=false due to legacy compatibility; dedicated+hosted true
Samir Rao: that could explain it. normalization toggle changes cache-keying so warmup misses.
Anya Patel: also saw higher eviction rates on private, latency to netstore is ~6-8ms vs 0.5ms on hosted.
Mike Chen: are private nodes using NFS-backed kvstore? or memcached?
Priya Singh: private = NFS netstore mounted in VPC + local in-memory LRU; hosted uses ram-native netstore
Jordan Lee: so warmup prefetch won’t fill keys before traffic bursts if netstore latency causes delays.
Samir Rao: also kernel change introduced padding of trailing newline in the input, which alters key hash in current keyer
Anya Patel: example keyer snippet:
```
key = sha256(prefix.strip().lower() + '::' + model_id + '::' + seq_len)
```
Priya Singh: people changed .strip() -> .rstrip() in the kernel rollout (a1b2c3) — subtle but breaks normalization
Mike Chen: can we run a microbench to simulate warmup with netstore latency and normalization off?
Jordan Lee: i'll run a 5k req replay with 200ms netstore delay, and capture hit rates + kernel traces
opsbot: scheduled job run-replay-1840111222 at 2026-03-18T15:12:00Z
infra-bot: perf profile uploaded: /artifacts/perf/1840111222/profile.html
Anya Patel: initial profiling shows batching heuristics also differ — private is batching more aggressively (higher batch sizes) which defers prefix cache lookups and increases misses on cold start
Mike Chen: why more aggressive? autoscaler config? batching.window_ms
Priya Singh: private had batching.window_ms=30 (to save GPU cycles), hosted = 10
Samir Rao: lowering window helps but increases GPU overhead. need a smarter heuristic: consider prefix-warmup state before batching
Jordan Lee: proposal: prefetch top-k cached prefixes during session init, and flag requests as 'warm' to bypass batching wait
Anya Patel: action items — (1) revert .rstrip change in kernel (rollback candidate), (2) patch private configs to enable prefix_normalize=true, (3) run replay + perf before/after, (4) evaluate prefetch prototype
Mike Chen: i'll own (1) & (3). Priya pick (2). Jordan & Samir prototype (4).
Priya Singh: noted.
Anya Patel: can we target canary on dedicated first? less risk
Mike Chen: yes — will deploy rollback to dedicated canary tomorrow 0900 UTC
Jordan Lee: i'll post replay results in this thread
Anya Patel: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
